youtube.title: Spaghetti rarely breaks in two | Reality Rulebook Season 2 · Episode 2
youtube.caption:
How many pieces? Bend a dry spaghetti stick until it snaps.

You expect two. You almost always get three or more. Slowed down, the first break sends ripples along the stick, and they bend it even more, so it snaps again. Then a team at MIT found a trick: twist the stick first, past about 250 degrees, and you usually get just two pieces.

Season 2 · Episode 2.

Sources
1. Heisser et al., 'Controlling fracture of brittle rods by twisting', PNAS 115, 8665 (2018); arXiv:1802.05402 (full text read by the builder, 9 Nov 2026): https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.05402
2. Audoly and Neukirch, 'Fragmentation of rods by cascading cracks: why spaghetti does not break in half', Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 095505 (2005) (not yet opened): https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.095505
3. c14 source as listed in claims.json: Phys. Rev. Lett. 58, 1038 (1987) (not yet opened): https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.1038
